label: Second copy step (output orig[1]) in long sequences, boosted when upcoming outputs are z/o/e/w/j/n
explanation: Fires only at the copy step with recall_idx == 1 (step L+1, input = orig(0), output = orig(1)); never in the original phase, at the delimiter, or at any other copy position. The firing rate rises steeply with L: about 0% for L<=5, 0.2% L=6, 0.7% L=7, and 32% of recall_idx==1 steps at L=9; L>=8 holds 85% of the mass. Inside that slot, whether and how strongly it fires depends on the upcoming tokens to be output (orig(1), orig(2), and to a lesser degree orig(3)). z is by far the strongest (out_tok z lift 7.3x, next_out z 8.3x), then o, e, j, n, w. The top activations are sequences like 1 z z z ... and x z z .... The identity of the input token orig(0) matters little. The effect looks like a graded, distributed token weighting, so a token-set predicate stops improving at about F1 0.54 on dev. The bare slot predicate (recall_idx==1) has recall 1.0 but precision 0.11.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: z, o, j, n, e, w; least: v, i, y, d) and the token being output (most: z, o, e, j, w, n; least: u, y, i, d); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=10, L=8 & t=9.
